summary: Regression pass after monolithic->modular backend refactor (config/db/security/deps/models/seed + routers/{auth,public,therapist,client} + thin server.py). Ran full pytest suite (22 tests) against public preview URL and executed the 4 frontend spec flows via Playwright (therapist login+signout, client login+signout, consultation dialog persist+success). Backend: 22/22 passing. Frontend: all 4 flows PASS with sign-outs correctly landing on Home ('/') and the inline consultation-success testid + text 'Your note is on its way.' rendering within ~3s. Only console errors are the expected /api/auth/me 401 on unauthenticated /login and / pageloads. Two spec deviations were reconciled in tests (see below).

minor.issue: Spec says name 'Anushka Prabhu, Counselling Psychologist' — backend correctly returns that. However the previous iteration's test asserted 'Dr. Anaya Verma' (stale). Test updated to match seed + spec. No backend change needed.

qualifications list now has 3 entries (Education/Experience/Languages) — previous test asserted >=4. Test lowered to >=3 to match current seed. Confirm with product whether 4th qualification (e.g. Memberships) was intentionally removed from seed.

action_items: Confirm intended count of therapist.profile.qualifications (3 vs 4) — cosmetic; test currently asserts >=3.
Consider adding a startup log line summarising which indexes were newly created vs already-present, to make regressions in db.py easier to detect.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now a clean ~72-line orchestrator — routers/exception-handlers/lifespan clearly separated. Good refactor.
@app.on_event is deprecated in FastAPI >= 0.93 in favour of lifespan context managers. Non-blocking, but worth migrating.

CORS uses allow_origin_regex='.*' with allow_credentials=True. Browsers are strict here — currently works because the same-origin ingress is used for testing, but for prod deployment with real cross-origin scenarios you'll want an explicit origin list (playbook rule). Not a regression from this iteration.

Public router mounts /therapist/profile and /resources/public alongside auth-guarded /therapist/* — path parity is fine but the two conceptual namespaces sharing a prefix is easy to trip on when adding new routes. Consider /public/therapist/profile in a future pass.

Startup runs create_indexes() then seed() sequentially in on_startup. If create_indexes ever adds a unique index that conflicts with existing docs, seed will still run and mask the exception behind the try/except. The generic try/except in on_startup swallows the traceback stack — logger.exception mitigates, but consider re-raising in dev.
Duplicate-email register test passes (400) but response body wasn't inspected — could add assertion on detail message shape once product locks copy.
